Cross-species synteny analyses revealed regions flanking 109 CMIs with conserved relative positions and transcriptional orientations across vertebrate genomes. As most of these loci reside within poorly annotated non-coding regions, we developed VertLncRNAchecker, a neural network-based web interface, that predicts lncRNA-like genes within these regions, which we termed positional ancestors. Finally, we validated in situ that these positional ancestors express mature lncRNA transcripts in the hearts of mice, pigs, and frogs, mirroring the expression of their human lncRNA counterparts. We present an accurate and retrainable computational platform for cross-species lncRNA discovery that prioritizes conserved genomic position over sequence conservation or existing genome annotations. This pipeline revealed putative ancestors of human heart-related lncRNAs hidden within the vertebrate non-coding dark genome, providing novel insights into lncRNA biology and evolution.

items.title_en: A robust mutation spectrum analysis framework for high-depth error-corrected sequencing data
items.title_zh: 面向高深度纠错测序数据的稳健突变谱分析框架
items.abstract_en: Comparing mutational spectra across experimental groups requires inference at the level of the biological replicate. Error-corrected sequencing (ECS) generates hundreds to thousands of mutations per replicate, yet classical pooled G2 tests treat individual mutations as independent observations and ignore replicate-level variability, inflating statistical significance (pseudo-replication). We present a replicate-aware Ridge-Penalized Dirichlet-Multinomial (RP-DMM) framework that models biological replicates directly and accounts for overdispersion. An L2 (ridge) penalty, with strength chosen by leave-one-out cross-validation, stabilizes spectrum estimates by shrinking weakly supported mutation categories toward a common baseline, and inference uses a parametric bootstrap. We also provide a complementary non-parametric rank-permutation test for sparse datasets. In simulations, the pooled G2 test became increasingly anti-conservative as mutation depth increased, with false-positive rates approaching 100% under the null hypothesis. RP-DMM maintained Type I error near the nominal 5% level and had substantially greater power than the rank-permutation test. Regularization was most consequential for high-dimensional spectra. False positive rates approached the nominal 5% level once the lower-mutation group contained approximately 300-500 mutations, depending on the number of biological replicates. A practical target of approximately 400 mutations in the lower-mutation group provided robust Type I error control across all scenarios examined; below this, the rank-permutation test performed robustly and is preferred. In Duplex Sequencing data from benzo[a]pyrene-exposed mice, RP-DMM distinguished exposure-associated mutational signatures from comparisons with higher mutation counts but null effect size, whereas the pooled G2 test declared all comparisons significant. The cross-validated penalty decreased as mutation depth increased, indicating that regularization strength should be tuned to the data. The framework is implemented in the MutSeqR R package.

items.title_en: DNA methylation reveals molecular heterogeneity and urate excretion-associated subtypes of gout
items.title_zh: DNA 甲基化揭示痛风的分子异质性及与尿酸排泄相关的亚型
items.abstract_en: Background: The molecular heterogeneity among gout patients remains largely unexplored, hindered the precise treatment for gout. Common indices for gout subtyping are cumbersome to measure, resulting in poor patient compliance. Methods: We elucidated the molecular heterogeneity of gout and developed a simple, reliable classification method for gout subtypes based on genome-wide DNA methylation, to facilitate individualized treatment. Genome-wide DNA methylation profiling was conducted in two independent cohorts, comprising a discovery cohort (n = 108) and a validation cohort (n = 100) representing four clinical gout subtypes. Results: We identified two gout subgroups associated with the fractional excretion of uric acid (FEUA) but not with 24-hour urinary uric acid levels (UUE) based on unsupervised clustering of whole-genome DNA methylation profiles, highlighting the contribution of epigenetic regulation to molecular heterogeneity in urate metabolism. Enrichment analysis links FEUA-associated subtypes to renal cell types, calcium related pathways and extended to the circulating immune compartment, with neutrophil- versus memory B cell-skewed leukocyte composition. A methylation-based classification model using 18 LASSO-selected CpGs with an XGBoost classifier effectively distinguished patients with high and low uric acid excretion, achieving excellent predictive performance (training cohort: AUC = 0.96, AP = 0.91; validation cohort: AUC = 0.86, AP = 0.85), outperforming the published model with clinical characteristics and SNPs. The signature site-associated genes NEK1 and TRPS1 display significant expression differences among urate-stratified patients and immune cells groups. TRPS1 may affect the AP-1/NF-{kappa}B inflammatory programme. Conclusions: These findings reveal distinct DNA methylation signatures underlying gout heterogeneity and demonstrate the feasibility of DNA methylation markers for gout subtype classification. The proposed methylation-based model provides a promising approach for personalized management of gout.

items.title_en: Predicting HPV/p16 Status and Molecular Subtypes from Histopathology Slides using Deep Learning in Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma
items.title_zh: 使用深度学习从组织病理学切片预测外阴鳞状细胞癌中的HPV/p16状态和分子亚型
items.abstract_en: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) comprises three prognostically distinct molecular subtypes: human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated, HPV-independent/p53-wildtype, and HPV-independent/p53-abnormal. Classification requires p16/p53 immunohistochemistry, which consumes tissue and is often incomplete in retrospective cohorts. We investigated whether deep learning could predict HPV/p16 status and molecular subtypes directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images. Using features extracted with H-optimus-1, we developed two attention-based multiple-instance learning models: HERA, predicting HPV/p16 status, and HERMES, predicting the three molecular subtypes. Models were developed on 644 patients from three Dutch VSCC cohorts and tested on 286 patients from two independent cohorts. In independent testing, HERA achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.84 (95% CI 0.75-0.91), with specificity 0.93, negative predictive value 0.94, and sensitivity 0.68. HERA-predicted groups reproduced the prognostic separation of HPV testing (log-rank p<0.001). HERMES achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.70 (0.66-0.75), with good discrimination for HPV-associated (0.80) but limited separation of HPV-independent/p53-abnormal (AUC 0.68) and HPV-independent/p53-wildtype (AUC 0.63). HERMES-predicted classes reproduced the prognostic hierarchy, with 5-year recurrence rates of 14.0% (HPV-associated), 31.1% (HPV-independent/p53-wildtype) and 43.3% (HPV-independent/p53-abnormal) (p=0.0051). Highly attended tiles showed basaloid cells and koilocytotic-like atypia in HPV-associated tumors, keratinizing nests with desmoplastic stroma in HPV-independent/p53-abnormal tumors, and well-differentiated keratinocytes with spongiosis in HPV-independent/p53-wildtype tumors. HERA could assign HPV/p16 status to large retrospective VSCC cohorts lacking ancillary testing, without consuming tissue, enabling HPV-stratified outcome analyses. Before such use, external validation of its discrimination and calibration across scanners and populations is required. HERMES suggests that molecular subtype information is encoded in hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides, but requires improved distinction between the HPV-independent subtypes.

items.title_en: Sex Differences Across the Donor Heart Offer-to-Outcome Pathway: A Linked National Cohort Study
items.title_zh: 供体心脏从邀约到结局路径中的性别差异：一项关联全国队列研究
items.abstract_en: Background: Sex differences occur across heart transplantation, but where they become apparent between donor-heart offers and post-transplant outcomes is uncertain. Methods: We linked UNOS STAR Q2 2025 candidate, donor, transplant, and PTR match-run data across pre- and post-2018 eras. Analyses included 51,970 listing episodes, 1,388,553 actual offers, and 38,417 recipients and evaluated access, conditional final acceptance, donor profiles, severe predicted heart mass (PHM) undersizing (ratio <0.86), treated rejection, and 365-day survival. Results: Transplant access increased in both sexes without evidence of sex-by-era modification (P=.133). Offers made to female candidates had higher adjusted conditional final-acceptance probabilities in both eras (interaction P=.172). After recipient-size standardization, severe PHM undersizing among realized offers remained less frequent for women than men pre-policy (28.9% vs 38.3%) and post-policy (25.5% vs 35.4%); acceptance of undersized offers was not lower for female candidates (three-way interaction P=.800). The threshold donor composite showed modest differences that reversed direction across eras. Adjusted treated rejection remained higher among women (male vs female OR, 0.667; 95% CI, 0.589-0.756), including after post-policy cPRA adjustment (OR, 0.678; 95% CI, 0.583-0.790). Adjusted post-policy 365-day survival was 91.0% in women and 92.3% in men; the sex difference did not change across eras (-0.64 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.97 to 0.68; P=.341). Conclusions: Sex-associated patterns were stage-specific and multidirectional. The final-graft PHM difference was already evident among realized offers after size standardization and was not explained solely by lower acceptance of undersized offers for female candidates. Women nonetheless had more treated rejection, while short-term survival differences did not change significantly across eras. Transplantation performance should be assessed separately across offer exposure, acceptance, matching, and outcomes.

items.title_en: Caesarean section in Bangladesh, 2012-13 to 2025: facility birth, the private sector and small-area geography
items.title_zh: 孟加拉国2012-13至2025年的剖宫产：机构分娩、私营部门和小区域地理
items.abstract_en: Background: In Bangladesh, caesarean section rose from one in five births in 2012-13 to one in two in 2025. We asked how much of this rise came from more facility births, a move to private facilities, and changing rates within sectors. Methods: This repeated cross-sectional study used Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys from 2012-13, 2019 and 2025 (26,539 recent mothers). A Kitagawa decomposition split the rise into parts. For 2025, we mapped caesarean use among facility births in 2,720 clusters and examined modelled travel time. Results: The caesarean rate rose from 19.5% (95% CI 18.1 to 20.9) to 52.0% (50.7 to 53.2). More facility births made up 82.8% (78.9 to 87.7) of this 32.5 point rise and the move to private facilities 12.6% (10.1 to 15.0). In a one-step version, place of birth made up 94.7% (90.7 to 98.9). The private caesarean rate rose from 79.1% to 86.1%, while the public rate fell from 38.7% to 33.5%. Among private first births, which rarely follow a previous caesarean, the 2025 rate was 4.8 points (0.3 to 10.2) above the 2012-13 model's prediction. The 2025 private rate was 85% to 87% in every wealth group. Longer travel time was linked with fewer caesareans, mainly through fewer facility births. Among private-sector births, travel time was not linked with caesarean (prevalence ratio 0.99 per 10 minutes, 0.97 to 1.01). Caesarean use among facility births clustered geographically; the private share of births in nearby clusters, not household factors, accounted for much of this. Conclusions: In accounting terms, most of the rise came from births moving into facilities, mostly private ones, where caesarean was already common. The data cannot show how many caesareans were needed. If 2025 sector mix and rates persist, more facility births would keep raising the national rate.

items.title_en: Community-Level Wastewater Surveillance of Nicotine Biomarkers Tracks Cardiovascular Disease Burden and Myocardial Infarction
items.title_zh: 社区级尼古丁生物标志物废水监测追踪心血管疾病负担与心肌梗死
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tobacco smoking is the largest modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet population-level surveillance still relies on self-reported and retail data, which are subject to measuring bias and lag. Urinary and salivary cotinine quantify individual tobacco exposure, but no analogous, objective metric exists at the community level. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has transformed surveillance of infectious diseases and illicit drug use; whether the same approach can yield a community-level signal of CVD risk is unknown. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to track community-level wastewater nicotine biomarkers and evaluate potential correlations with relative CVD burden in El Paso, Texas. METHODS: We integrated wastewater nicotine biomarker surveillance with electronic health record (EHR) data across four sewersheds in El Paso, Texas. Twenty-four-hour composite influent samples were collected monthly (June 2024 to May 2025; n=48) and quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for five nicotine metabolites. Cotinine, nornicotine, and trans-3-hydroxycotinine (3HC) were detected in 91.6 to 100% of samples, whereas tobacco-specific nitrosamines were below limit of detection. CVD cases (January 2021 to December 2024) were obtained from the Paso del Norte Health Information Exchange and mapped to sewersheds by residential ZIP code using ArcGIS. At the sewershed level, population normalized nicotine mass loads tracked the proportional burden of atherosclerosis/ischemia/infarction and heart failure. Across the sewersheds, monthly 3HC mass load and the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR) were strongly and specifically associated with incident ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) (3HC vs. STEMI: rho=0.893,p=0.012), without parallel associations for non-ST elevation or old myocardial infarction. CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that integrating wastewater nicotine surveillance with EHR data can reveal community-level 3HC and NMR as specific indicators of incident STEMI. Our findings indicate wastewater surveillance as a novel, objective tool to inform cessation policy and CVD prevention

items.title_en: USFDA Oncology Drug Approvals from 2014- 2025: Comparing non-immunotherapy and immunotherapy approvals, their endpoints, and their efficacy.
items.title_zh: 2014-2025年USFDA肿瘤药物批准：比较非免疫治疗与免疫治疗批准、其终点及疗效
items.abstract_en: In the United States the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and in Europe, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) are responsible for regulatory approvals of anti-cancer therapeutics. We examined regulatory approvals by both agencies in the period between 2014 and 2025 and compared immunotherapy and non-immunotherapy approvals for the treatment of cancer. We asked whether the approvals were similar in terms of trial size, endpoints, and development time. We present the data based on the FDA approvals given that the US agency has approved some therapies either rejected by or yet to be approved by the EMA. Beginning with the approval of pembrolizumab for melanoma in 2014 through early 2025 we identified 143 immunotherapy and 211 non-immunotherapy approvals. In the first few years the time to approvals of immunotherapies was markedly less but over time the duration has approached that of non-immunotherapies - with durations of 2079 and 2357 days in 2024/2025 due largely to a median trial size of 461 and 698 participants. Surrogate endpoints have overwhelmed overall survival as the primary endpoint for approval, and we find that with non-immunotherapies only a median of 60% of the benefit predicted from progression/disease/recurrence/event-free survivals translates to overall survival, significantly less than the 99% of the surrogate benefit translated to overall survival for immunotherapies. While the FDA and EMA approval portfolios are very similar, the EMA is on the whole more skeptical/conservative in its approvals. The last decade has seen substantial advances, but much remains to be accomplished against a formidable foe. The size and duration of trials need to be addressed and meaningfully reduced and the validity of surrogates defended.

items.title_en: Trajectories and characteristics of pain in the first year after spinal cord injury: a TRACK-SCI study
items.title_zh: 脊髓损伤后第一年疼痛的轨迹与特征：一项TRACK-SCI研究
items.abstract_en: Chronic pain affects most individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) and frequently impairs daily function, and nearly half experience neuropathic pain. Neuropathic pain is commonly thought to develop months after injury and to persist once established. These views rest on classifying each patient as having neuropathic pain or not, although patients often report several pains. The same binary label is the usual target of prognostic and biomarker studies that aim to predict life-limiting pain. We tracked up to three of the worst pains per interview from injury to one year in 140 TRACK-SCI participants, using the DN4 interview (DN4i, threshold 3). Within three days of injury, half of all pain areas and three quarters of participants met the threshold, and pain-area prevalence changed little over the year. Individual pains, however, often changed. Only a third remained above the threshold throughout, one third resolved or fluctuated, and pains in the same person often followed different courses. At more than half of interviews with several pains, one pain met the threshold while another did not, so that the patient's classification depended on the pain considered. We therefore derived a threshold-free Pain Composite Score from the DN4i items and pain intensity. The items formed a single dimension, and the composite was associated with sleep and mood interference whereas the binary classification was not. Neuropathic pain after SCI thus appears early, does not invariably persist, and differs between a person's pains, and graded pain-level measures may offer a more stable target for predicting life-limiting pain.

items.title_en: Relevance-Based Prediction: A Transparent, Patient-Specific Approach to Predicting Medical Outcomes
items.title_zh: 基于相关性的预测：一种透明、患者特定的医学结局预测方法
items.abstract_en: Accurate prediction of individual medical outcomes is essential for optimizing treatment allocation amid rising costs, coverage denials, and limited clinical resources. Traditional predictive models, including linear regression and neural networks, rely on average effects and cannot tailor predictions to the specific circumstances of individual cases. We present relevance-based prediction (RBP), a model-free and task-specific method that predicts outcomes as weighted averages of observed cases, with weights determined by a rigorously defined and theoretically justified measure of relevance. Unlike model-based methods that rely on fixed calibrated parameters, relevance-based prediction revisits the original data for each prediction and customizes both the cases and variables used. We illustrate RBP by applying it to predict opioid treatment outcomes and demonstrate that it provides case-specific insights unavailable from conventional models, including how each prior case informs a prediction, how each variable affects each predictions reliability and value, and how reliable each prediction is before it is made. These individualized insights may prevent misleading average-based decisions and reduce harmful or suboptimal treatment.

items.title_en: Source-water salinity measured by electrical conductivity in Bangladesh, 2025: a nationally representative cross-sectional survey
items.abstract_en: BackgroundIn coastal Bangladesh, saline drinking water has been linked to raised blood pressure. The 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) measured electrical conductivity (EC), a salinity indicator, in source water, but its report gave no population counts or district estimates. ObjectivesTo estimate how many people live in households whose tested source has high EC, and to describe patterns by place, household characteristics, source type and arsenic. MethodsEC was measured in source water of 6,040 households in 64 districts, February to June. In 14.5% of households the tested source was not the main drinking-water source. Primary outcomes were EC above 1,500 and 3,000 {micro}S/cm, survey risk classes that are not health-based standards. Estimates were survey weighted; comparisons were observational. ResultsEC exceeded 1,500 {micro}S/cm in 5.3% of households (95% CI 4.7 to 5.9), about 9.0 million people, including 1.8 million above 3,000 {micro}S/cm. Coastal-zone districts held 26% of households but 70% of those above 1,500 {micro}S/cm. Shares varied little by wealth or in households with young children or pregnant women. Nationally, deep tube wells more often had high EC because most are coastal. In the coastal zone, deep and shallow wells had similar shares (16.1% and 17.9%). After district adjustment, EC was about 18% lower in deep wells (geometric mean ratio 0.82, 0.73 to 0.92). Within upazilas (restricted sample) it was 0.93 (0.80 to 1.07). Arsenic above 10 ppb was more common where EC was high, but this link weakened after district adjustment. ConclusionsMillions of people live in households whose tested source has high EC, mostly in coastal and south-central districts. Deep wells had modestly lower EC after geographic adjustment, but the difference shrank within upazilas and depended on the handling of implausibly low readings. The findings support measuring EC alongside arsenic, with documented meter calibration.

items.title_en: Patient-keyed aggregation of public cancer genomic data imports clonal hematopoiesis into solid-tumor mutation matrices
items.abstract_en: Large-scale reuse of public cancer genomic data begins by pooling studies into one patient-by-gene matrix, keyed on the patient. Records held under one patient identifier need not come from the same kind of specimen: three clonal-hematopoiesis studies in cBioPortal deposit blood normals sharing patient identifiers with tumors deposited elsewhere, so a patient-keyed merge records a hematopoietic clone as a tumor mutation. We linked 1,282,483 coding calls in 140 genes from 483 studies to patients, classified each by specimen type, and rebuilt the matrix with and without blood-derived calls. Blood normals supply 1.7% of calls but concentrate: 52.8% of patients flagged DNMT3A-mutant, 21.3% of TET2 and 19.7% of CHEK2 have no tumor-derived call in that gene, against 0.4% for TP53. Those calls carry a hematopoietic gene spectrum and, in TP53, hematopoietic allele fractions. The artifact reaches 65 further cohorts, almost all solid-tumor studies, exceeding one patient in ten in fifteen of them, and tracks the share of patients with a paired blood normal, not the disease (r = 0.994, 45 cancer types). Correction lowers the pan-cancer DNMT3A rate by 45% and moves survival estimates further than chance removal of the same patients would. Two filter lines applied before aggregation remove it.

items.title_en: Dynamics of random recurrent neural networks: colored noise and sublinear activations
items.abstract_en: We study the dynamics of recurrent neural networks with random couplings, sublinear odd activation functions, and temporally correlated noise. Using large N methods, we determine stationary correlations and distinguish the loss of local linear stability from the onset of chaos, characterized by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent. These thresholds delimit an intermediate regime in which local instability coexists with asymptotic stability under a common noise history. Their separation depends on both the noise correlation time and the asymptotic growth of the activation function. We show that internal noise with any finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the network's intrinsic correlation time tau_corr at the edge of chaos; it exhibits a critical scaling tau_{corr,max} propto 1/sqrt{D_0}, where D_0 is the integrated noise strength. Static random input instead produces coincident thresholds and a divergent correlation time. We also calculate the frequency-dependent participation dimension from a four-point correlation function. Its zero-frequency value is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the network correlation time, predicting a smooth minimum at the weak-noise chaos threshold. Numerical simulations support the large-network predictions and reveal appreciable finite-size effects.

items.title_en: Benchmarking Recent Single-Cell Synthetic Data Generation Methods on the OneK1K Dataset
items.title_zh: 在 OneK1K 数据集上基准评测近期单细胞合成数据生成方法
items.abstract_en: Synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generation offers a promising route for privacy-aware biomedical data sharing, but donor-linked datasets require careful balancing of biological utility and privacy risk. In this work, we benchmark synthetic generation methods for the CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health Privacy Challenge using the donor-split OneK1K dataset, comparing scGFT, scLDM, and Cell2Sentence across statistical fidelity, downstream biological preservation, and membership inference vulnerability. Because full-transcriptome generation is computationally demanding, we focus generative modeling on highly variable genes and evaluate alternative strategies for reconstructing non-HVG expression. Our results show that non-HVG handling is a central determinant of privacy: directly copying non-HVG values leads to severe leakage, whereas Poisson-based reconstruction substantially reduces membership inference risk. We further find that scGFT and scLDM better preserve biological structure than an independent Poisson baseline, while maintaining near-random privacy profiles under appropriate configurations. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating synthetic single-cell data beyond marginal similarity alone, emphasizing robustness, interpretability, and privacy-conscious design choices throughout preprocessing, generation, and post-processing.
items.abstract_zh: 合成单细胞 RNA-seq 数据可支持隐私友好的数据共享，但供体关联数据需权衡生物学效用与隐私风险。本文针对 CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health 隐私挑战赛，基于按供体划分的 OneK1K 数据集，从统计保真度、下游生物学信息保留和成员推断脆弱性三方面评测 scGFT、scLDM 与 Cell2Sentence。因全转录组生成代价高，建模聚焦高变基因，并比较非高变基因表达的重建策略。结果显示：直接复制非高变基因数值会造成严重泄漏，而基于泊松的重建可显著降低成员推断风险；scGFT 与 scLDM 在适当配置下比独立泊松基线更好地保留生物结构，隐私表现接近随机。
items.highlight_zh: 非高变基因的处理方式决定合成数据的隐私风险
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：单细胞 RNA 测序数据高度敏感，直接共享会暴露供体身份，合成数据是兼顾共享与隐私的方案。但数据既要"像真的"（保留生物学信号），又不能"太像"（让人反推出真实供体），二者需要权衡。
② 方法：作者以按供体划分的 OneK1K 数据集为基准，在 CAMDA 2026 ELSA Health 隐私挑战赛框架下比较三种生成方法——scGFT、scLDM 和 Cell2Sentence。评估分三方面：统计保真度、下游生物学分析是否仍成立、以及成员推断攻击（攻击者能否判断某供体数据是否参与了训练）。由于逐基因生成整个转录组计算量太大，只对高变基因做生成建模，并单独设计非高变基因表达的重建策略。
③ 结果：非高变基因怎么补，是决定隐私成败的关键——直接照抄原始数值会造成严重信息泄漏；改用泊松分布重建则大幅降低成员推断风险。在合适配置下，scGFT 与 scLDM 比"独立泊松"基线更好地保留生物结构，同时隐私指标接近随机猜测。
④ 意义：说明评价合成单细胞数据不能只看总体分布相似度，还要在预处理、生成、后处理全链条上做隐私友好设计，并报告鲁棒性与可解释性。

items.title_en: Music Between Two Minds: Individual Signatures, Shared States, and the Emergence of Creative Interaction
items.abstract_en: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown. Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes. Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos. Improvising pairs thus neither fuse into one system nor remain two independent ones: they preserve individual melodic voices while sharing a rhythmic state, within which moment-to-moment push-pull continually rebalances their interaction. Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

items.title_en: Confinement of hybridized light modes in nonlinear-optical superpotentials
items.title_zh: 非线性光学超势中杂化光模式的局域化
items.abstract_en: In this work, we present a spatial and temporal light trapping mechanism induced by coherent frequency conversion. We consider a wave-mixing process, where a pumped nonlinearity mediates a frequency-domain beamsplitter interaction between two signal modes. When these wave modes are counterpropagating, temporally trapped eigenmodes emerge at the zero of the nonlinearity profile. We establish that such spatio-temporal trapping has a direct connection to supersymmetric quantum mechanics, which ensures the existence and robustness of the trapped modes and allows us to derive analytic solutions of the bound eigenmodes. Backwards sum-frequency conversion may thus enable a unique class of active photonic memory devices, whose design parameters are compatible with the state of the art in integrated nonlinear photonics. We propose proof-of-principle experiments to study this nonlinear-optical trapping effect on thin-film lithium niobate. In addition, as a case study, we show how the temporal trap can be used alongside parametric gain. Our work unveils potential applications ranging from classical integrated photonics to multimode quantum nonlinear photonics.
items.abstract_zh: 本文提出一种由相干频率转换诱导的空间与时间光捕获机制。我们考虑泵浦非线性介导两个信号模式之间频域分束器相互作用的混波过程；当两个波模式反向传播时，在非线性分布零点处会出现时间上被捕获的本征模式。我们证明这种时空捕获与超对称量子力学有直接联系，后者保证了捕获模式的存在性与鲁棒性，并使我们能导出束缚本征模式的解析解。反向和频转换有望实现一类独特的有源光子存储器件，其设计参数与集成非线性光子学现状兼容。我们提出在薄膜铌酸锂上开展原理验证实验，并以参量增益为例展示时间陷阱的用法。
items.highlight_zh: 借超对称量子力学实现光的时间捕获并给出解析解
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：能否在集成光子芯片上把光"困住"一段时间，用作光存储器？作者提出用非线性频率转换（混波过程）实现空间与时间上的光捕获。
② 方法：考虑一个泵浦非线性过程，它在两个信号模式的频率之间起到"分束器"作用。当两个信号模式反向传播时，在非线性强度分布的零点处会出现时间上被束缚的本征模式。关键是作者发现这一现象与超对称量子力学（supersymmetric quantum mechanics）直接对应：该数学结构既保证了束缚模式的存在与鲁棒性，也允许写出解析解。
③ 结果：给出了束缚本征模的解析形式；指出反向和频转换可实现一类"有源"光子存储器件，其参数与当前集成非线性光子学工艺兼容；提出在薄膜铌酸锂（thin-film lithium niobate）平台做原理验证实验，并展示时间陷阱与参量增益结合使用的案例。
④ 意义：把超对称数学工具引入非线性光学，为集成光存储、模式操控乃至多模量子非线性光学提供新思路。

items.title_en: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
items.title_zh: 量子参数估计究竟估计什么？关于"真实量值"的不可能性结果
items.abstract_en: We examine the conditions under which quantum parameter estimation is compatible with the concept of a ``true'' quantity value: a unique value of the estimated quantity that exists prior to and independently of measurement. While quantum parameter estimation typically assumes that the quantity to be estimated is a parameter, we argue that this assumption can be lifted, opening the way to a more general formulation of estimation that may apply even in situations where the quantity to be estimated is no longer a parameter, but instead a quantum variable susceptible to quantum fluctuations. We identify three assumptions that characterize the way estimation is often presented in the quantum metrology literature, namely, as a procedure for inferring an unknown ``true value", which is assumed to be unique and to exist prior to and independently of measurement. Using our more general framework, we prove a no-go theorem showing that the preceding assumptions are jointly incompatible with two further assumptions: the completeness of the quantum state (no `hidden variables'), and the presence of entanglement between the probe systems and the system under measurement. We note that the presence of such entanglement is a generic prediction of standard quantum theory. Consequently, if one is not willing to accept hidden variables, nor willing to modify standard quantum theory by introducing a new physical mechanism that destroys entanglement at some scale or regime, then a realist account of estimation is ultimately impossible.
items.abstract_zh: 我们考察量子参数估计与"真实量值"概念相容的条件，即被估计量存在唯一且先于、独立于测量的取值。传统参数估计假定被估计量是一个参数，本文主张放弃该假定，给出更一般的估计框架，使其也适用于被估计量为受量子涨落影响的量子变量的情形。我们提炼出文献中常隐含的三条假定；基于更一般的框架，我们证明一个不可能定理：这三条假定与量子态完备性（无隐变量）以及探针与被测系统间的纠缠不能同时成立，而该纠缠是标准量子理论的普遍预言。因此，若既不接受隐变量、也不修改标准量子理论，实在论的估计解释终归不可能。
items.highlight_zh: 证明"真实值"实在论解释与标准量子理论不相容
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：量子计量学（如估计相位、磁场强度）通常被描述为"推断某个客观存在的真实值"。但量子力学中，被估计的量未必是一个固定参数——它可能与探针纠缠、本身有量子涨落，测量前并没有确定取值。那么"参数估计"究竟在估计什么？
② 方法：作者先把估计框架从"估计参数"推广到"估计量子变量"，再梳理文献中隐含的三条实在论假定：存在唯一真值、真值先于测量存在、真值独立于测量。然后在此一般框架下证明一个不可能（no-go）定理。
③ 结果：这三条假定与另外两条假定不能同时成立——量子态的完备性（不存在隐变量），以及探针系统与被测系统之间存在纠缠。而纠缠恰恰是标准量子理论的普遍预言，并非特例。因此：若不愿接受隐变量，也不愿引入在某个尺度上破坏纠缠的新机制来修改标准量子理论，就无法对估计给出实在论解释。
④ 意义：这是一项概念性基础工作，厘清了量子参数估计的语言与前提，提醒人们在解释精度极限（如海森堡极限）时不要默认"真值客观存在"这一经典直觉。

items.title_en: GEM-PIC-RZ: a Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell code in quasi-cylindrical geometry with nonuniform grids
items.title_zh: GEM-PIC-RZ：准柱坐标下带非均匀网格的伽利略电磁粒子模拟程序
items.abstract_en: Laser-plasma accelerators span scales from the micrometre wavelength of the driving laser to acceleration lengths of millimetres or metres. Full particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations resolve the laser carrier but are constrained by the Courant condition, whereas quasi-static models are computationally efficient but do not resolve it. We present GEM-PIC-RZ, a quasi-cylindrical implementation of the Galilean electromagnetic PIC scheme. The method retains the slow evolution of the forward field and therefore resolves the laser carrier while allowing a propagation step governed by the evolution of the laser and plasma rather than by the cell size. User-defined nonuniform grids and a charge-conserving regularization of the bubble closure support efficient simulations across these scales. Comparisons with the full PIC code FBPIC show agreement for the laser wake, the depletion and redshift of a few-cycle pulse, and ionization injection; the measured CPU time is about 2\,\% of that for FBPIC in the reported runs; the injected charge carries a model uncertainty of about 15\,\% from the regularization. An envelope model, in contrast, underestimates the depletion of the few-cycle pulse fivefold. Self-injection in a sharp density down-ramp is not yet reproduced and remains an open problem.
items.abstract_zh: 激光等离子体加速器跨越从驱动激光的微米波长到毫米乃至米的加速长度。全粒子模拟（PIC）可分辨激光载波，但受 Courant 条件限制；准静态模型计算高效却分辨不了载波。我们提出 GEM-PIC-RZ，即伽利略电磁 PIC 格式的准柱坐标实现。该方法保留前向场的慢演化，因而可分辨激光载波，同时允许推进步长由激光与等离子体的演化而非网格尺寸决定。用户自定义非均匀网格与泡闭合的电荷守恒正则化支持跨尺度高效模拟。与全 PIC 程序 FBPIC 的比较显示，激光尾波、少周期脉冲的损耗与红移以及电离注入均一致；所报告算例中 CPU 时间约为 FBPIC 的 2%；正则化带来的注入电荷模型不确定度约 15%。相比之下，包络模型将少周期脉冲损耗低估五倍。陡峭密度下降沿处的自注入尚未复现，仍为开放问题。
items.highlight_zh: 准柱坐标伽利略 PIC：可分辨激光载波且快约50倍
items.digest_zh:
① 研究问题：激光等离子体加速器的尺度跨度极大——驱动激光波长只有微米量级，加速长度却可达毫米甚至米。全粒子（PIC）模拟能分辨激光载波，但步长受 Courant 条件限制，计算极其昂贵；准静态或包络模型虽快，却丢掉了载波信息。
② 方法：作者提出 GEM-PIC-RZ，把伽利略电磁 PIC 格式实现在准柱坐标（RZ，轴对称）几何中。它保留前向传播场的慢演化，因此仍能分辨激光载波，但推进步长由激光和等离子体的演化尺度决定，而不再受网格尺寸约束。程序还支持用户自定义非均匀网格，并对"泡"（bubble）闭合关系做电荷守恒的正则化处理。
③ 结果：与全 PIC 程序 FBPIC 的对比显示，激光尾波结构、少周期脉冲的损耗与红移、以及电离注入均吻合；在所报告算例中 CPU 时间仅为 FBPIC 的约 2%；正则化使注入电荷带有约 15% 的模型不确定度；相比之下包络模型把少周期脉冲损耗低估了约 5 倍。方法尚未复现陡峭密度下降沿处的自注入，这是待解决的开放问题。
④ 意义：为跨尺度激光等离子体加速模拟提供了既分辨载波又高效的数值工具，但自注入等强非线性过程仍需进一步改进。

items.title_en: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
items.title_zh: 利用量子模拟筛选固体氧化物电池中的强关联材料
items.abstract_en: We develop an end-to-end framework for assessing a quantum-computing application in industrial materials science: the screening of strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials for SOFCs and SOECs. We formulate the materials problem in terms of interface observables including oxygen-vacancy formation energies, vacancy migration barriers, and electronic conductivity. We describe how these observables can be obtained using a diagrammatic GW-based embedding, either GW+DMFT or self-energy embedding theory (SEET), applied to a DFT-screened shortlist. The atomistic electrode/electrolyte interface defines the electronic structure problem from which the correlated impurity models are constructed. Quantum impurity solvers would provide the finite-temperature impurity Green's functions required by the embedding. The computational challenges that classical solvers may encounter as the interacting active space grows, together with the polynomial scaling of quantum Hamiltonian simulation for efficiently represented discretized models, open an opportunity for quantum advantage. We identify the benchmarks needed to assess this opportunity through convergence of vacancy and migration energetics and comparison with the best applicable classical solvers. We provide illustrative logical qubit counts and identify the thermal state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated-solve costs needed for a complete resource assessment. We connect microscopic observables to macroscopic engineering metrics using a continuum model for mixed ionic--electronic conducting oxygen electrodes that couples oxygen surface exchange, solid-state oxygen transport, electrode microstructure, and finite electrode thickness. Finally, we estimate the potential worldwide business value of improved electrode materials under SOFC and SOEC deployment scenarios informed by public technical targets and electrolyser deployment data.

items.title_en: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
items.title_zh: 通用量子误差下的混合态深度热化
items.abstract_en: Pure-state deep thermalization predicts that, after sufficient scrambling, projected ensembles approach universal distributions that contain information beyond the reduced density matrix. In realistic quantum systems, however, noise is unavoidable and the projected states are generally mixed. Whether mixed-state deep thermalization admits an analogous universal limiting distribution has remained unclear. Here we answer this question for quantum dynamics containing local quantum channels, i.e., errors. We show that the late-time mixed-state projected ensemble is completely determined by the normalized Choi state of the error channel and is universal, independent of the microscopic details of the underlying unitary dynamics. We establish this result analytically for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar-random dynamics, and local Haar-random circuits at large local dimension, and verify it numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics. In a solvable setting, we further find exponentially fast convergence to the limiting ensemble. Our results extend deep thermalization to noisy quantum dynamics and establish a direct correspondence between quantum errors and universal random mixed-state ensembles.

items.title_en: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
items.title_zh: 量子Gibbs采样器的尺寸无关对数Sobolev不等式
items.abstract_en: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. We apply it to two regimes: one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature, and finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

items.title_en: ArcTN: Efficient Tensor-Network Contraction Planning for Quantum Circuit Simulation
items.title_zh: ArcTN：用于量子电路仿真的高效张量网络收缩规划
items.abstract_en: Tensor-network simulation of quantum circuits depends on contraction orders with low computational cost and small intermediate tensors, found without excessive planning time. We present ArcTN, a contraction-order optimization framework with two search presets. Light keeps planning overhead low, and Heavy spends more effort on refinement. Both combine randomized-greedy construction, subtree reconfiguration, and parallel tempering with stage-specific stopping rules. ArcTN also provides Fixed and Dynamic slicing to meet tensor-size limits and executes the returned orders. On the 30 QC32 quantum-circuit networks completed by all eight compared configurations, Light reduces FLOPs by 61.32% and plans 1.62$\times$ faster than Cotengra Auto/CMA-ES, and Heavy reduces FLOPs by 43.83% and plans 7.21$\times$ faster than Cotengra AutoHQ/Optuna. Heavy also needs 11.85% fewer FLOPs than OMECO TreeSA-8 and plans 1.33$\times$ faster. Dynamic slicing meets the size limits in all 90 runs on 18 scalar-output networks and reduces total sliced FLOPs by 31.99% relative to Fixed slicing, at the cost of longer planning. With a common NumPy executor, Heavy has the lowest combined planning and execution time among five configurations on the runs that all of them completed. On 672 networks built from 320 MQT Bench circuits, Heavy obtains the lowest geometric-mean FLOPs on the 142 large networks while planning 3.1$\times$ and 31$\times$ faster than Cotengra AutoHQ and Hyper128.

items.title_en: Problem-aware sampling for bias and variance reduction in randomised Hamiltonian simulation
items.title_zh: 用于随机化哈密顿量模拟中偏差与方差降低的问题感知采样
items.abstract_en: Randomised quantum simulation algorithms such as qDRIFT reduce circuit depth by replacing deterministic product formulas with stochastic compilations, but achieving high accuracy can require many steps. In vanilla qDRIFT, Hamiltonian terms are sampled with probabilities proportional to their coefficient magnitudes. We propose StateDRIFT, a variant of qDRIFT which optimises its sampling distribution to estimate time-evolved quantities using knowledge of the initial state and target observable, with a provable truncation bound that keeps qDRIFT's guarantees. The distribution at each depth is chosen by solving an optimisation problem targeting bias and/or variance. StateDRIFT can significantly reduce the bias and variance of estimators, and hence circuit depth, which we test on short-time dynamics of lattice models and molecules under Jordan-Wigner up to 18 qubits. For example, with BeH2 StateDRIFT can reduce the number of two-qubit gates required to achieve a given accuracy from 11,201 to 983. StateDRIFT involves measuring observables and commutators on the initial state, so we propose two practical ways to estimate these: classical surrogates such as tensor networks, and classical shadows, which recover most or all of the saving from exact oracles in the systems tested.

items.title_en: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
items.title_zh: 基于Petz恢复与二元假设检验的单次纠缠生成与蒸馏
items.abstract_en: How much entanglement can two distant laboratories share when their connection is noisy? We relate this question to deciding which of two quantum hypotheses is present. Our one-shot bounds apply to entanglement generation over a quantum channel and to one-way entanglement distillation from a shared state. We use Cheng's trace inequality to bound the infidelity of a Petz decoder in terms of a binary hypothesis testing cost. Applying the inequality before averaging over codes reduces the error analysis to computing a second moment of random subspaces. The proof covers every integer target dimension and treats rank-deficient states explicitly. A corollary expresses the achievable entanglement through hypothesis-testing coherent information, with a single logarithmic error slack and exact integer rounding. We also prove an error-preserving conversion from entanglement generation codes to entanglement transmission codes: the target dimension decreases by only a constant factor at fixed error, and the decoder is the original decoder followed by local processing. Consequently, for both entanglement generation and entanglement transmission, arbitrary pure reference-input states yield the same coherent-information rate, second-order Gaussian correction at the original error tolerance, and explicit achievable logarithmic remainder. For commuting testing hypotheses, the logarithmic remainder improves to a constant. These results give a direct route from binary distinguishability to explicit recovery guarantees and finite-resource quantum communication rates.

items.title_en: The Impact of Markovian Errors on Random Circuits
items.title_zh: 马尔可夫误差对随机电路的影响
items.abstract_en: Randomized benchmarking (RB) returns a single decay parameter or gate error rate, but when the noise is gate-dependent that parameter is notoriously difficult to interpret. We study RB and related random-circuit benchmarks under small gate-local Markovian noise by factorizing each noisy gate into its ideal action followed by the exponential of a small error generator and then perturbing the RB $\mathscr{L}$ matrix, which models the RB decay. For any low-error gate set that satisfies the requirements of RB (it is a sequence-asymptotic unitary 2-design), we show that Pauli-stochastic error rates contribute linearly to the RB decay parameter, while Hamiltonian error rates contribute through a gauge-invariant quadratic form. Pauli-correlation and active generators are absent from the linear term and enter only at higher order. For the single-qubit native gate set $\{X_{π/2},Y_{π/2}\}$ we derive this quadratic form explicitly in terms of three first-order gauge-invariant (FOGI) coordinates: the two intrinsic over-rotations and one relational axis-tilt error. The resulting formula explains the dependence of DRB on the sampling distribution and the compilation dependence of CRB. These results turn RB decay rates into interpretable functions of experimentally meaningful elementary error rates.

items.title_en: Observation of Polarization Topology in Magneto-Optical BICs
items.title_zh: 磁光BIC中偏振拓扑的观测
items.abstract_en: Polarization topology in momentum space is a fundamental characteristic of photonic bound states in the continuum (BICs), where the winding of far-field polarization defines a quantized topological charge. Although magneto-optical (MO) BICs combine polarization topology with magnetically tunable chirality, experimental characterization remains challenging because time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking complicates eigenpolarization extraction. Here, we experimentally resolve the momentum-space polarization topology of an MO BIC by reconstructing its two-dimensional far-field eigenpolarization texture. We extract the resonant output polarization using singular value decomposition of the polarization-resolved angle-resolved reflection matrix without invoking reciprocity. The reconstructed polarization azimuth winds counterclockwise by 2$π$ around the $Γ$-point singularity, yielding a topological charge of q = +1. Moreover, the polarization handedness can be reversed solely by varying the magnetic-bias strength, while the field direction and the measured topological charge remain unchanged. A non-Hermitian coupled-mode model traces this reversal to hybridization between the BIC mode and a leaky mode. This work establishes experimental access to momentum-space polarization topology in nonreciprocal photonics, opening a route to explore topological singularities and their evolution under active TRS breaking.

items.title_en: Nanopillar metasurfaces uniting high optical reflectivity with ultracoherent nanomechanics
items.title_zh: 纳米柱超表面将高光学反射率与超相干纳米力学相结合
items.abstract_en: Mechanically compliant mirrors are key components in cavity optomechanics. However, the requirements to achieve the best optical and mechanical performance are usually in direct competition. A high reflectivity for tightly focused beams entails thick reflectors, whereas ultracoherent flexural nanomechanics necessitates thin membranes. We eliminate this trade-off by introducing high-refractive-index nanopillar metasurfaces on top of a thin membrane. We pattern a 50 micrometer-diameter array of nanopillars to form a photonic crystal. The flat band behavior of guided resonances in the photonic crystal enables a reflectivity of 99.82(1)% for a tightly focused beam of 7 micrometer waist. The combination of two guided resonances creates a 100 nanometer-wide high-reflectivity band around 1550 nanometer. Simultaneously, the nanopillar patterning realizes a density-modulated phononic crystal that isolates an ultracoherent localized mechanical mode with a $Q\cdot f$-product of $2\cdot 10^{14}$Hz. The demonstrated nanopillar metasurfaces enable lightweight mirrors for room-temperature quantum optomechanics and for use as levitated mirrors or lightsails.

items.title_en: ConQEC: Concolic Testing for Quantum Error-Correcting Code Implementations
items.title_zh: ConQEC：面向量子纠错码实现的Concolic测试
items.abstract_en: Quantum error-correcting code (QECC) implementations are hybrid software-control systems: measured syndromes drive decoder dispatch, recovery actions, and logical checks. Existing QECC verification techniques can prove formal obligations, and general quantum testing can expose final failures, but developers still lack a scalable testing workflow that generates concrete faults and explains where a QECC repair path first diverges. This paper presents ConQEC, to our knowledge the first concolic testing framework for QECC implementations. By combining concrete (Pauli) fault replay with symbolic repair-path constraints, ConQEC generates tests that expose not only final logical failures but also fault--syndrome--decoder--recovery (FSDR) diagnostics: the injected fault, observed syndrome, decoder decision, recovery action, oracle result, and earliest divergent stage. Its symbolic encoding of Pauli faults, syndrome predicates, decoder and recovery relations, and oracle checks enables this diagnostic workflow to scale beyond exponentially increasing amplitude-level quantum-state reasoning. We implemented ConQEC and evaluated it on generated source-level QECC families and public QECC artifacts with up to thousands of qubits. ConQEC detects the seeded bug in every experimental case and reports a replay-valid, fault-localizing FSDR witness for each.

items.title_en: Nonlinear quantum noise polarization in macroscopic nonlinear QED
items.title_zh: 宏观非线性QED中的非线性量子噪声偏振
items.abstract_en: We construct a quantum theory of light in nonlinearly responding materials with dispersion and absorption and, in particular, show the emergence of non-Gaussian noise associated with nonlinear absorption processes. Our theory is based on a path-integral formulation of the microscopic Huttner-Barnett model including cubic matter self-interaction required for $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinear processes. We show that the noise polarization emerges naturally from a decoupling of the stochastic weights of the bath response which, in case of cubic self-interactions, leads to a decoupling via Airy functions. As the theory is, by construction, consistent with the nonlinear fluctuation-dissipation theorem, it constitutes a viable quantum theory of light in nonlinear media.

items.title_en: Predictive electronic feedback control for narrow-linewidth lasers
items.title_zh: 窄线宽激光器的预测型电子反馈控制
items.abstract_en: Narrow-linewidth lasers are essential for various key atom-laser interaction processes and optical setups in quantum coherent control, quantum precision measurement, and quantum information science. The Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) technique is the standard method for the frequency-stabilization of narrow-linewidth lasers, but the inherent time delay in its feedback loop inevitably induces excessive phase noise, commonly known as servo bumps. Previous solutions primarily rely on additional optical components outside the electronic feedback control loop. Here, we propose and implement a generic method based on the Smith predictor to address the time-delay issue entirely within the electronic part of the PDH feedback control loop. We systematically demonstrate its capability to suppress phase noise and reduce servo bumps by adding only a single Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) controller to the loop. This class of methods is demonstrated to be conceptually concise with minimal hardware overhead, effective in practice, and holds potential for a wide variety of future applications.

items.title_en: Krylov Complexity and Entropy of Composite Quantum Systems
items.title_zh: 复合量子系统的Krylov复杂度与熵
items.abstract_en: We investigate the behaviour of Krylov complexity as the number of degrees of freedom of a quantum system increases. Specifically, we show that for tensor products of commuting subsystems, the leading excess complexity is controlled by a weighted variance of the subsystem Lanczos coefficients. This provides a quantitative measure of dynamical heterogeneity and a precise characterization of synchronous evolution. We also show that Krylov entropy is able to disambiguate the information associated with subsystems composition from that generated by dynamical mismatch, and that the same Lanczos variance controls the leading mismatch contribution to both complexity and the entropy. Our results establish excess complexity and Krylov entropy as complementary probes of the emergence of collective dynamics in large quantum systems.

items.title_en: Qubits Are Not Enough: Deflation and Measurement Limits in Variational Quantum Modal Analysis
items.title_zh: 量子比特还不够：变分量子模态分析中的Deflation与测量限制
items.abstract_en: Amplitude encoding stores an N-degree-of-freedom structural mode using ceiling(log2 N) qubits. This article develops an evaluation framework for variational quantum eigensolvers in finite-element structural dynamics. A Cholesky transformation maps the generalized eigenproblem to a symmetric mass-orthonormal Hamiltonian, ensuring Euclidean quantum-state orthogonality equals structural mass orthogonality. For higher modes, the deflation penalty condition is sharpened to a necessary-and-sufficient threshold, with a Davis-Kahan bound quantifying effects of approximate projectors. Numerical studies separate mapping correctness, ansatz expressibility, preprocessing, Pauli growth, finite-shot uncertainty, and damage localization. For 128-DOF chains, consistent-mass whitening increases transformed-operator density from 0.023 to 0.308 and Pauli terms from 576 to 2950. Exact state-vector experiments show qubit count and circuit expressibility are distinct. At 10^5 shots per Pauli term, first-mode frequency RMS error is 2.45%. In an oracle-state study, 10% stiffness loss is localized in 84.5% of trials. Results sharpen the deflation condition, quantify resource bottlenecks, and claim no speedup.

items.title_en: Orbital-coherence memory in electrical transport and its self-consistent Maxwell response
items.title_zh: 电输运中的轨道相干记忆及其自洽麦克斯韦响应
items.abstract_en: An internal electronic coherence changes electrical transport only when it feeds back on the physical current. We develop a reduced description of this feedback and distinguish its exact consequences from the assumptions required for a microscopic realization. An opposite-parity two-orbital Hamiltonian identifies a current-coupled orbital force. Under an explicitly stated moment closure and collision ansatz, it yields a passive three-state response with an exponentially damped oscillatory memory. The resulting conductivity redistributes a fixed optical weight and predicts a nonmonotonic dependence of dc conduction on coherence damping at fixed remaining parameters. The orbital reduction constrains the coupling and internal frequency through a shared bare splitting, providing a test beyond unconstrained spectral fitting. A charge-conserving spatial extension couples to Maxwell equations through a positive energy balance and separates the constitutive response from longitudinal collective and transverse electromagnetic modes. We formulate complex-conductivity and transmission tests, including the limits of parameter identification over a finite bandwidth. The model supplies a conditional connection between orbital dynamics, transport memory, and electromagnetic observables; conductivity alone does not establish a uniquely quantum mechanism, and a material-specific collision calculation and closure-error assessment remain necessary.

items.title_en: Finite Systems in the Space of Projective Measurements
items.abstract_en: We investigate the dynamics of two-level systems using the quasidistribution $Q$ function projected onto the space of collective measurements. Particular attention is given to evolution under Hamiltonians that are invariant under particle permutations, for pure states that are either invariant or noninvariant under such permutations. This requires constructing an approximate analog of the star product between quasidistribution functions: the projected $Q$ function of a product of two operators is expressed approximately in terms of the individual operators' $Q$ and $P$ functions. We rewrite the Liouville equation to determine approximate state dynamics and compare the result with exact evolution using the Hellinger distance. Overall, the method performs well for permutation-invariant pure states and Hamiltonians, whereas deviations arise for arbitrary pure states and noninvariant Hamiltonians.

items.title_en: Automating quantum circuit optimization with AI agents
items.abstract_en: Compiling quantum algorithms for real devices involves hard optimization problems that can decide whether an algorithm runs at scale. We present a general method for solving such problems with AI agents, with every result certified. It builds on autoresearch loops, in which agents iteratively improve programs against a fixed evaluator and which have recently improved quantum cryptanalysis circuits, and adds two elements: a frozen, exact verifier certifies every result, and this verifier, together with the challenge around it, is built by an agent that formulates the problem with a researcher and validates the verifier against a solved case, deliberately broken solutions and published results before any solution exists. The method applies to any optimization problem whose solutions can be verified exactly and efficiently. We apply it to three compilation problems in quantum simulation, namely fermion-to-qubit encoding, Hamiltonian layout and unitary synthesis. In each, the agents improved substantially on published or standard constructions, reducing the cost being optimized by up to 73% at the largest sizes tested and outperforming a state-of-the-art optimizer for fermion-to-qubit encodings. Every submission is a program accompanied by its agent's notes, so the ideas behind each improvement are recorded in human-readable form; later agents built on them, and we describe them here. These results open the way to automated, certified discovery across quantum circuit design and beyond.

items.title_en: Quantum Fokker-Planck solvers as trainable generative models
items.title_zh: 量子 Fokker-Planck 求解器作为可训练生成模型
items.abstract_en: We develop and analyze generative models based on quantum solvers of stochastic differential equations. Unlike the common approach based on layered variational quantum circuits with parameterized rotations, we parameterize the potential of a Langevin process. The associated Fokker-Planck (FP) equations are Hermitianized and solved using a linear combination of cosine operators implemented through quantum singular value transformation. By encoding the square root of the stationary density, the model enables sampling through computational-basis measurements and is efficiently controlled by coefficients of the block-encoded diagonal potential. We train the proposed model to match empirical distributions within the family described by FP equations, demonstrating parameter recovery for multivariate probability distributions. Crucially, the model remains trainable at scale. Sample-efficient and convex optimization for in-distribution targets arises from a physics-informed inductive bias and holds regardless of the dimensionality of the problem. We provide circuit constructions and efficient block encodings of the main components of the algorithm and analyze resource requirements. Our approach frames quantum generative learning as quantum model discovery and provides a foundation for extending this framework to high-dimensional, strongly correlated scientific data.

items.title_en: A New Twist on Astigmatic Transformation: Beyond Laguerre-Gaussian Beams
items.abstract_en: Astigmatic transformation is widely used to convert the azimuthal phase structure of Laguerre-Gaussian vortex beams into intensity patterns from which the topological charge can be read out. Here, we show that this phase-to-intensity conversion is not just restricted to the Laguerre-Gaussian radial profile. We derive analytical expressions for the astigmatically transformed high-order Bessel--Gauss and perfect optical vortex fields, and find that, despite their substantially different radial structures, the number of intensity minima is directly set by the accumulated azimuthal phase winding. Numerical simulations and experimental measurements on both beam families confirm this result, establishing astigmatic transformation as a direct probe of the topological charge of scalar structured optical fields. We further extend the approach to non-separable vector Bessel-Gauss beams, in which the spatial and polarization degrees of freedom are coupled, and show that polarization-resolved detection allows the topological charge of the constituent spatial modes to be determined independently.

items.title_en: High-fidelity entanglement of two spectrally-distinct solid state emitters
items.title_zh: 两个光谱可区分的固态发射器的高保真纠缠
items.abstract_en: Solid state quantum emitters with electronic spin properties can be entangled using optical interferometric which-path erasure techniques that rely on identical frequencies and linewidths of the emitters. This promises a powerful, fast and scalable platform for quantum technologies. Using current protocols, a pair of emitters embedded in a waveguide interferometer can be deterministically prepared in a maximally entangled state. However, the amount of entanglement diminishes rapidly with increasing separation of the emission lines and variations in the linewidths of the emitters. Solid state emitters such as quantum dots are subject to intrinsic variations in the fabrication process. Therefore, manufacturing the required number of identical emitters on a chip is not scalable. In this Letter, we present a method that uses readily available pairs of entangled photons to entangle solid state emitters with large transition frequency separations and linewidth variations, circumventing the need to fabricate optically identical emitters. We demonstrate a concurrence of C = 0.95 for typical quantum dots using narrowband photon inputs.

items.title_en: Rank-One Loss Maximizes the Spectral Response Strength of Passive Full-Order Exceptional Points
items.abstract_en: We consider finite-dimensional non-Hermitian systems in which all modes coalesce at a single exceptional point. For a rank-one anti-Hermitian contribution, the spectral response strength is computed exactly. For passive systems, we then derive a sharp upper bound at fixed exceptional-point decay rate and show that it is reached only when the decay operator has rank one, corresponding to a single independent dissipative direction. This establishes rank-one loss as the optimal configuration for enhancing the response of a full-order exceptional point. The bound holds for arbitrary order and improves on earlier passive estimates beyond second order. Two third-order trimers illustrate the result: a rank-one-loss system saturates the bound, whereas a passive rank-two-loss realization remains below it. The result turns dissipation into a design resource: concentrating the loss into a single effective dissipative direction maximizes the highest-order spectral response of a passive full-order exceptional-point device.

items.title_en: Can Entanglement-Induced Feature-Map Designs Improve Projected Quantum Kernels?
items.title_zh: 纠缠诱导的特征图设计能否改进投影量子核？
items.abstract_en: Projected quantum kernels (PQKs) have emerged as a notable approach to circumvent the hardness of machine learning tasks arising from the exponential dimensionality of the quantum Hilbert space. However, recent PQK studies often rely heavily on extensive classical hyperparameter tuning of the radial basis function (RBF) kernel parameter and the support vector machine regularization parameter. The extensive tuning can mask the true representational power of the underlying PQKs induced by quantum feature maps, which has not been explored in detail. Thus, this work aims to expose the structural capabilities of PQKs by isolating and evaluating their native inductive bias through comparisons between untuned and tuned PQKs against the RBF baseline. Furthermore, we propose novel quantum feature maps that leverage two-qubit entanglement to capture multivariate correlations in IoT data. The results show that extensive tuning can lead to competitive performance architectures, while our proposed entanglement topologies exhibit a significantly stronger native inductive bias. This reveals that superior quantum architectural design can yield structurally better PQKs with improvements arising from quantum-mechanical properties rather than from classical hyperparameter tuning.

items.title_en: Reset-Enhanced Dissipative Quantum Metrology
items.abstract_en: Quantum metrology is ultimately shaped not only by measurements, but also by the dissipative dynamics that prepare and maintain the probe. Nevertheless, a general mechanism for enhancing both steady-state and transient precision in open quantum systems has been lacking. Here we show that adding a simple reset channel provides such a mechanism: reset acts as a minimal dissipative control that can enhance metrological precision without modifying the intrinsic Hamiltonian or applying continuous coherent driving. We derive a unified quantum-Fisher-information (QFI) reset-rate response identity, showing how reset enhances steady-state and transient estimation while revealing a sharp transient distinction. For static-parameter estimation in diagonal dynamics, reset leaves the leading short-time QFI unchanged; for the separate task of elapsed-time estimation, it generates an immediate drift contribution that can scale quadratically with the reset rate in the short-time limit. For frequency estimation, the enhancement is instead dominated by a genuinely quantum eigenvector contribution. These results establish reset as a simple dissipative resource for open-system quantum metrology.

items.title_en: Second- and third-order nonlinearities in silicon nitride waveguides via heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate membranes
items.title_zh: 通过铌酸锂薄膜异质集成实现氮化硅波导中的二阶和三阶非线性
items.abstract_en: Thick, dispersion-engineered silicon nitride is a leading platform for integrated third-order nonlinear optics, supporting supercontinuum and frequency comb generation. However, it lacks the second-order nonlinearity required by many applications. Here we bond pre-fabricated x-cut thin-film lithium niobate membranes onto finished silicon nitride waveguides as a back-end step, compatible with commercially fabricated waveguides. A single silicon nitride waveguide generates an octave-spanning supercontinuum and, through the lithium niobate membrane, concurrent second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation. These results open new possibilities for thick silicon nitride photonics, from visible light generation to on-chip $f$-$2f$ comb self-referencing, a key step towards miniaturised timing and navigation quantum technologies.

items.title_en: Fluctuation-free Quantum Battery Charging Enabled by Bell-like Entangled and Separable Charger States
items.abstract_en: The implication of entanglement in quantum battery charging remains poorly understood. In addition, intrinsic quantum randomness poses a fundamental challenge to charging uniformity across distinct trials. To address these issues, we study a three-qubit system within a cascaded collision frame, with two qubits acting as the charger and the third serving as the battery. After each collision, an adaptive measurement is performed on the charger, yielding four conditional post-measurement battery states with identical expected stored energy. For arbitrary fixed charger states, we derive analytical expressions for the recurrence relation of stored energy. We find that stored-energy fluctuations depend on whether the dynamics relies on the battery phase \(γ_n\). For two Bell-like families of entangled states, together with their computational basis states termed Bell-like separable states, the dynamics is \(γ_n\)-independent and fluctuations vanish, whereas for other entangled and separable states, fluctuations emerge. These insights establish a paradigm for engineering charger states to design uniform-charging quantum-battery architectures despite inherent quantum randomness.

items.title_en: Local Dephasing Sustains Continuous Time Crystals in a Spin-1/2 Ensemble
items.abstract_en: Local pure dephasing suppresses single-spin coherence, yet we show that it sustains continuous time-crystalline order in a fully connected ferromagnetic spin-$1/2$ ensemble with local decay. An exact operator identity reveals the mechanism: dephasing raises the interaction energy, while energy relaxation on a finite timescale converts this charging into delayed feedback. Within homogeneous mean-field theory, we prove that dephasing is necessary for periodic motion in this model and that feedback exactly balances transverse damping over each cycle. Beyond mean field, the identity fixes the relative amplitude and phase of energy and longitudinal magnetization in oscillatory Liouvillian modes. Liouvillian spectra and stationary two-time correlations characterize temporal order through decay rates that decrease algebraically with system size, frequencies approaching nonzero mean-field values, and comparable per-spin oscillatory weights. Semiclassical trajectories further reveal recurrent switching between a limit-cycle region and two symmetry-related stationary regions: fluctuations interrupt and reactivate collective oscillations, and oscillatory episodes provide an intermediate channel between stationary regions. These results establish local dephasing as a resource for autonomous collective motion and show how the resulting temporal order can participate in metastable dynamics.

items.title_en: Shaping Near Fields of Photonic Modes into Topological Textures
items.abstract_en: Topological textures of light, such as optical vortices and skyrmions, are attractive for high-density information encoding and light-matter interactions. In the near field, topologies have primarily been realized using polaritonic platforms that inherently tie the platform to the material dispersion, limiting their footprint due to propagation losses and restricting their operating spectral region. Here, we introduce a route to shape near-field topologies through the geometric engineering of a dielectric metasurface supporting a quasi-bound state in the continuum resonance, without the need for polaritonic surface waves. In-plane deformation of our metasurface bars conserves their resonance-driven near-fields locally, so that the metasurface geometry and the polarization of the illuminating light dictate the generated topology. By shaping silicon unit cells into geometries with rotational symmetry, we create optical topologies with controllable topological charge. Using phase-resolved scattering-type near-field optical microscopy, we experimentally characterize high-purity resonance-locked topologies such as vortices in concentric rings and topological charge doublets in Archimedean spirals. In contrast to conventional topological textures, our purely photonic mode-based field textures are stationary standing waves in the radial direction, without relying on surface-wave propagation or polaritonic dispersion, establishing a spectrally and spatially scalable platform for near-field topological photonics.

items.title_en: Entanglement certification of attosecond light fields with photoelectron interferometry
items.abstract_en: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

items.title_en: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
items.abstract_en: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

items.title_en: Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent
items.abstract_en: We propose Quantum Constrained Hamiltonian Descent (QCHD), a continuous-time quantum framework for optimization under smooth equality constraints. The unconstrained counterpart, Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD), minimizes a cost function by simulating the Schrödinger dynamics of a particle in the potential given by the cost function. Applying Dirac's formalism to the classical dynamics with constraints, we construct an intrinsic quantum Hamiltonian with a Laplace--Beltrami operator on the constraint manifold in a kinetic term. Its evolution preserves the constraints exactly without penalty terms and is expected to solve quantum-dynamically the constrained optimization problem. We analyze its relation to Quantum Hamiltonian Descent supplemented by a strong penalty term. For a squared-distance penalty, the effective tangential dynamics acquires an extrinsic-curvature potential and, in nontrivial normal-rotation sectors, a coupling to the normal-bundle connection. These embedding-dependent terms remain in the strong-penalty limit, generally yielding quantum dynamics different from QCHD. Numerical comparisons for circular, elliptical, and two simultaneous constraints show faster optimization and improved concentration near global minima for the initial states and finite penalty strengths considered.

items.title_en: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
items.abstract_en: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.

items.title_en: The limits of magic-state distillation
items.abstract_en: Magic-state factories are a major cost of fault-tolerant quantum computing, yet how few noisy inputs they need is known only for restricted protocols. We show that, for tolerating input faults, any stabilizer protocol, however adaptive, postselected or multistage, is no better than a projection onto one stabilizer code, and that for rational targets a fault pattern is harmful exactly when its complement is. Searches over all codes show that quadratic distillation of one T state needs exactly nine inputs and that the eight-input CCZ factory is optimal. At order $d$, one T state needs $n\geq2d$.

items.title_en: Norm-Aware Product Formulas for Hamiltonian Simulations
items.abstract_en: With the target of efficiently solving the quantum-mechanical Schrödinger equation on future quantum computers, first- and second-order product formulas for the time-evolution operator are proposed, designed to exploit hierarchies in the operator norms of the individual Hamiltonian components. Inspired by the THRIFT product formula, these decomposition schemes achieve a suppression of the leading error term by a factor of alpha<1 with respect to the standard Lie--Trotter--Suzuki splitting of the same order, where alpha quantifies the norm ratio between the dominant and subdominant parts of the Hamiltonian. Unlike THRIFT, the proposed formulas retain the general product-formula structure, making them applicable to Hamiltonians whose terms act on an arbitrary number of qubits. The advantages of this approach are demonstrated through numerical experiments on engineered two-dimensional spin-1/2 XY model systems and isolated molecules within the double-factorization framework.

items.title_en: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
items.abstract_en: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states.
